# Composio toolkit research: 100 apps

Machine-readable data: data.json (same folder).

## Patterns
- OAuth 2.0 dominates, but keys are the fast lane. 72/100 apps offer OAuth 2.0 and 23 are key/token-only. 55 of the 72 OAuth apps <i>also</i> issue a personal key or token, so a toolkit can ship on keys first and add OAuth for multi-tenant use. The OAuth-only ones include the app-review platforms (Google Ads, LinkedIn, Amazon, Pinterest, Threads) and accounting (QuickBooks, Xero).
- 73/100 are self-serve (57 free, 16 via free trial). The gates are concentrated. 8 need platform app review (WhatsApp Business, Google Ads, Meta Ads, LinkedIn Ads, Pinterest, Threads (Meta), Squarespace, Amazon Selling Partner). 8 are partner / contact-sales (DealCloud, Gladly, Salesforce Commerce Cloud, Waterfall.io, Clay, Paygent Connect, PitchBook, Consensus), and 11 need a paid plan.
- Openness tracks category. Fully open: Developer, Infra and Data platforms (10/10), Productivity and Project Management (10/10). Most gated: Marketing, Ads, Email and Social (5/10, mostly app review / approval), AI, Research and Media-native (5/10, mostly paid plan).
- The #1 blocker is commercial, not technical. Enterprise contract / customer account (14), Platform app review / approval (11), Paid plan required (7). Only 5 apps are truly blocked today; 63 are ready and 32 are buildable with a caveat.
- MCP is already mainstream. 73/100 apps ship an official MCP server and 14 more have community ones. Several gated or API-less products (Clay, Otter, DealCloud, iPayX) now expose MCP before, or instead of, a broad REST API.
- 63 easy wins vs 16 need outreach. Easy wins are self-serve, documented and verdict ready; outreach means partnership, app review or a contract.
